qwen.ref_text: On the battlefield, four players with monster-like strength appeared. Each of the players had already destroyed their colonies. These players were so equally strong, they created a four-way deadlock.

lines: Lecture seven. Swarm intelligence. This is how many simple ants can find short routes together.
A colony is made of many ants, all identical and simple.
A colony is many identical, simple ants.
Each ant only reacts to what is near it.
Each one only reacts to what is near it.
There is nobody in the middle. No leader gives the orders.
No leader gives the orders.
Yet together, the ants can find short routes. This is called emergent behaviour.
Together they can find short routes.
One scout ant is right sixty percent of the time.
One scout ant is right 60% of the time.
Now eleven scouts vote for a route, and the colony follows the majority.
Eleven scouts each vote for a route.
The majority is right seventy-five percent of the time.
The majority is right 75% of the time.
With thirty-one scouts, that climbs to eighty-seven percent.
With 31 scouts it climbs to 87%.
In the double bridge experiment, ants reach food by either of two equal bridges.
Ants use either of two equal bridges.
At first, the ants choose at random.
At first the ants choose at random.
Ants leave pheromone, and they prefer the stronger trail.
Ants leave pheromone and prefer strong trails.
Soon most ants use one bridge.
Soon most ants use one bridge.
Which one comes down to chance. These colonies settle on opposite bridges.
Which one is down to chance.
Now the experiment again, with one road twice as long.
One road is twice as long.
The ants walk at the same speed, so the short trip ends first.
Same speed: the short trip ends first.
Its pheromone is laid sooner, so more ants pick that road.
More pheromone, so more ants pick it.
Soon most ants take the short road.
Soon most ants take the short road.
In two hundred colonies, eighty-five percent end up on the short road.
85% of 200 colonies pick the short road.
A few lock onto the long road, through early bad luck.
A few lock onto the long road.
An ant walks from the nest to the food, and leaves a scent mark.
An ant leaves a scent mark on the ground.
A later ant senses it, and follows.
A later ant senses it and follows.
Communicating through marks in the environment is called stigmergy.
That is stigmergy.
For ants, the scent is only a sign, not the work itself.
Scent is a sign, not the work.
Sometimes the work itself prompts others, as a growing pile attracts builders.
The work itself can prompt others.
Each step, the ants using a trail add pheromone to it.
Each step, ants add pheromone.
Each step, a fifth of the pheromone evaporates.
Each step, a fifth of it evaporates.
The trail levels off where gain equals loss. Four ants a step give twenty, and two give ten.
It levels off where gain equals loss.
A new ant picks by share. Twenty out of thirty is sixty-seven percent, so stronger trails win.
Stronger trails get picked more.
If the ants stop, the trail fades away.
If the ants stop, the trail fades away.
Now the ants meet a map. An ant must visit all four towns, then go home.
Goal: visit every town, then go home.
At town A, each unvisited town gets a weight: pheromone divided by distance.
Weight = pheromone ÷ distance.
The weights become chances, and the ant picks by chance. Here it picks C.
A random pick, by those chances.
A tour memory stops the ant visiting a town twice.
Tour memory stops repeat visits.
From C it picks B, then only D is left. Then it goes home.
It visits every town, then goes home.
The tour length is four plus six plus three plus five, which makes eighteen.
Tour length: 4 + 6 + 3 + 5 = 18.
The tour is done, so now the trails update, in two steps.
Tour done. Now the trails update.
First, evaporation. In this example, every road keeps half of its pheromone.
In this example, each road keeps half.
Second, deposit. Each tour road gains Q divided by the length. Seventy-two divided by eighteen is four.
Then each tour road gains Q ÷ length.
Roads the ant skipped only lose pheromone.
Skipped roads only lose pheromone.
Now many ants go round the map, one after another, each using the same update.
Ants go round one after another.
Ant six finds a shorter tour, so it adds about five to each road, against four for the long tours.
A shorter tour adds more to each road.
So the trail leans towards the shortest tour. It takes the lead, and keeps it.
So the trail leans towards the shortest tour.
The first five ants walked only long tours, yet the short tour wins in the end.
The first ants found only long tours.
Simple ants with no boss can make a clever colony.
Trails build up, fade away, and guide the next ant.
Short routes get more pheromone, so they win.
